findings.title: Concurrency test never requests subgroup counts and does not exercise getSubGroupsCount
findings.body: The call `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)` passes true as `briefRepresentation`; the separate `subGroupsCount` parameter remains at its default false. `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount`, and therefore `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount`, is only invoked when subgroup counts are requested. As written, this regression test would pass even without the production change because the code path that produced the NPE is never executed. The test needs to issue the list request with `subGroupsCount=true` while deletes are happening.

findings.title: Reader thread is never joined or reliably stopped
findings.body: The test starts a non-daemon thread that loops while `deletedAll` is false. `deletedAll.set(true)` is only reached after the delete loop at line 155, so if any `remove()` call throws, the flag is never set and the reader thread keeps issuing requests forever, potentially preventing the test JVM from terminating. Even on the success path the assertion at line 157 runs without joining the reader, so a request already in flight can still add an exception to `caughtExceptions` after the assertion or continue running into the next test. The delete loop should be wrapped in try/finally, the reader must always be signalled to stop, and the test should join/await it before asserting.

findings.title: No synchronization ensures the reader thread performs any read during deletion
findings.body: After `Thread.start()` returns, the main thread immediately starts deleting all 100 groups and then sets `deletedAll`. Scheduling is not guaranteed: the reader may first observe the flag after it has already been set, so its loop body never executes and the test passes without performing any concurrent read. A latch or barrier should ensure the reader has entered at least one list request while groups are being deleted, plus a completion signal so the test can wait for it.
